name: Fermented vegetables
standfirst: Every one of these is a raw vegetable kept from the air until the bacteria already on its skin turn it sour. What separates them is how the salt gets in, what goes in with it, how cold it is kept and for how long — and whether you stop while it still cracks.
root: Raw vegetable · packed away from the air · the lactic bacteria already on it

nestings.label: By how the salt goes in

dishes.name: Sauerkraut
dishes.note: No brine is poured in. The salt pulls one out of the cabbage, and the weight holds the cabbage under it — that is the whole trick.

dishes.name: Suan cai
dishes.note: Whole napa heads rather than shreds, and cold enough that the ferment takes all winter instead of a month. Sauerkraut reached independently.

dishes.name: Ogórki kiszone
dishes.note: The horseradish leaf is not seasoning. Its tannins slow the enzymes that soften the cucumber — the one ingredient here whose job is texture.

dishes.name: Kimchi
dishes.note: The only one salted twice over: brined to draw water out, rinsed so it is not inedible, then packed with a paste that ferments alongside it.

dishes.name: Dongchimi
dishes.note: Not kimchi minus the paste — it is older than chilli in Korea. The liquid is strained off for cold noodle broth.

dishes.name: Pao cai

salt: never touched with an oily hand

dishes.note: The jar has a water moat round its lid: gas escapes, air never gets back in. The old brine is kept going for decades and inoculates each new batch.

dishes.name: Zha cai
dishes.note: The knobbed stem of a mustard plant, not a leaf. Pressing it three times is what leaves it crunchy after half a year in the jar.

dishes.name: Nukazuke

salt: buried in a wet rice-bran bed
add: a bran bed kept alive for years

dishes.note: The bed is the dish and the vegetable is a guest — cucumbers go in at night and come out at breakfast, and the nukadoko is fed and stirred forever.

dishes.name: Dưa cải chua
dishes.note: Mustard greens, wilted a few hours so they bend into the jar. The rice water and the sugar are both there to get the bacteria moving before anything else does.

dishes.name: Torshi left
dishes.note: Turnip. The beetroot is one slice and it is there entirely for the colour. The Persian sense of torshi usually means vinegar instead — this is the salt-brine branch.

dishes.name: Şalgam suyu

end: the vegetable is only the flavouring

dishes.note: The turnip and black carrot are strained out and the brine is served cold beside kebab. The one entry here where the pickle is thrown away.

dishes.name: Kanji
dishes.note: Black carrot fermented into a sour drink, set out in the winter sun to keep the jar warm — the same answer Adana arrived at, with mustard doing the work of the bulgur.

dishes.name: Gajar gobhi shalgam achar
dishes.note: The winter pickle. Oil on top does what a brine does elsewhere — seals the surface — and the jaggery gives the bacteria something to eat.

dishes.name: Curtido
dishes.note: Three days, not three weeks, so it is a relish rather than a preserve. The scald is argued over — skip it and the ferment starts faster.

dishes.name: Gundruk
dishes.note: No salt anywhere in it. Bruising the leaves floods the pot with their own juice fast enough that nothing else gets a foothold — then it is sun-dried and keeps for a year.

dishes.name: Gari
dishes.note: Cassava, and the ferment is not for flavour — it breaks down the cyanide that makes the raw root poisonous. Toasting on a hot pan ends it.

notes.title: On salt
notes.body: Salt ferments nothing. It pulls water out of the vegetable into a brine that lactobacillus tolerates and most spoilage organisms do not — it is a doorman, not a cook. Brining and dry-salting are two routes to the same brine: one you mix, the other the cabbage makes. Gundruk and gari dismiss the doorman entirely and rely on speed and an airtight pot instead.

notes.title: On where you stop
notes.body: Crunch is pectin, and pectin is lost to warmth and time rather than to salt. The same jar of cucumbers is a crisp half-sour at three days on the counter and a soft full-sour at three weeks, with nothing added in between. Everything in the crunchy column is cold, or fast, or both.

notes.title: On depth
notes.body: Nothing here sits under anything else. Kimchi is not dongchimi with chilli paste added — dongchimi is older than chilli in Korea, and both descend from the same salted radish. Sauerkraut and suan cai are one idea arrived at twice by people who never met. Siblings, all of them.
